chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is standing in prayer and sees a louse; he said, 'Let him bury it in the pebbles, for indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say, 'When you see it, bury it in al-Batha'.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they see a louse while standing in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the fiqh of minor distractions during Salah, specifically the ruling on killing a louse found on the body. It prescribes burying the louse in pebbles or the ground rather than crushing it, thereby preserving the validity of the prayer by avoiding the major distraction of killing. The narration links this practice to Imam Ali (peace be upon him), citing 'al-Batha' (often identified as the open ground near Mecca or Medina) as the traditional location for such burial, reflecting the Shia emphasis on emulating the Imams' practical jurisprudence.
